name: Corroded Shrapnel
summary: In Stonetalon, jagged metal remains lodged deep inside corrupted treants. The Venture Company’s retreating munitions left fragments in the forest’s protectors, now sought for study.

sections.title: Remnants of Industrial Ruin
sections.body: When the Venture Company was driven from Stonetalon’s groves, its goblins used reckless munitions to cover their escape. Explosive shrapnel tore into the valley’s defending treants, lodging deep within their bark and core. The ancient guardians slowly succumbed to corruption. Their wood blackened, and their fury turned against anyone entering the vale. Kaela Shadowspear seeks the rusted fragments so Gaxim Rustfizzle, a gnome, can study how the weapons brought on the treants’ corruption.

faq.q: Where does this shrapnel come from?
faq.answer: The shrapnel comes from corrupted treants in the Stonetalon Mountains, including Charred Ancients, Blackened Ancients, and Vengeful Ancients.

faq.q: Why is the shrapnel embedded in the treants?
aliases: how did shrapnel get in treants
why are treants full of metal
faq.answer: The Venture Company’s explosive munitions struck the treants as the forest guardians drove goblin loggers from the vale. Shards lodged in their bark during the battle and remained there.

faq.q: Is the shrapnel responsible for corrupting the forest ancients?
faq.answer: Kaela Shadowspear says the gnome Gaxim believes the treants’ corruption is tied to the foul chemical or metallic makeup of the retreating goblins’ weapons.

faq.q: Who wants to inspect the shrapnel?
faq.answer: Kaela Shadowspear, a night elf, wants a sample to pass to Gaxim, a gnome inventor who plans to study its properties and learn what afflicts the treants.

angles.text: As a druid, seeing Kalimdor’s ancients warped by goblin munitions and festering metal shards shows the cost unchecked exploitation brings to the wild.
As a gnome, you can see Gaxim’s study of tainted shrapnel as a practical, scientific way to investigate an ecological mystery that woodland sentinels cannot explain.
